title: The Mustard Seed
review_status: DRAFT: retelling and wondering questions require theological and editorial review before release.

source.note: Original child-friendly retelling written for this prototype; not a quotation of any translation. See also Matthew 13:31-32 and Luke 13:18-19.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: This is a story Jesus told. Let's carry the story box to the table, and listen.

segments.text: Jesus wanted people to know what the Kingdom of God is like. He said, "What is it like? What story can we tell?"
"It is like a mustard seed. A mustard seed is one of the smallest seeds of all. It is smaller than a crumb!"
Someone took the tiny seed and planted it in the ground.
And it grew. Day and night, little by little, it grew.
It grew until it was bigger than all the other plants in the garden, with big, strong branches.
It grew so big that the birds came and made their nests in its shade.

wonderings: I wonder how something so small can become so great.
I wonder if the seed knew what it would become.
I wonder who the birds might be.
I wonder what the Kingdom of God is like.

steps.prompt: When you're ready, put each piece back in its place in the box.

feedback.mismatch: That spot is for a different piece.
feedback.all_good: Every piece is back in its place.

outro.speaker: narrator
outro.text: The story box is back on the shelf. You can come back to it whenever you like.

journal_line: I listened to the story of the mustard seed and watched it grow into a great plant with birds in its branches.
